title: MCO Q3 Earnings Miss Estimates as Costs Rise & MIS Revenues Fall
author: Na
description: Moody's reported Q3 2026 adjusted earnings of $4.14 per share, missing the consensus estimate of $4.25, though earnings grew 6% year-over-year. Revenues rose 1% to $2.02B but fell short of expectations. The results were pressured by increased operating expenses and a 1% decline in Moody's Investors Service revenues due to lower leveraged finance issuance, partially offset by 3% growth in Moody's Analytics. The company reaffirmed its 2026 guidance.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Earnings and revenue both missed consensus estimates. Operating expenses increased 2% year-over-year, pressuring margins. Moody's Investors Service revenues declined 1% due to lower leveraged finance issuance. Stock fell nearly 3% in pre-market trading on the weaker-than-expected performance.
Reported Q4 fiscal 2026 results that beat both earnings and revenue consensus estimates. Earnings grew 8.6% year-over-year and revenues increased 6.2%, demonstrating strong operational performance.

Scheduled to report Q3 2026 results on Oct. 27. Consensus estimate for quarterly earnings has been revised higher to $4.43, but this represents a 6.3% decline from the prior-year quarter, indicating mixed expectations.

title: Analysts Estimate S&P Global (SPGI) to Report a Decline in Earnings: What to Look Out for
author: Zacks.Com
description: S&P Global is expected to report a year-over-year decline in earnings and revenues for Q3 2026, with consensus EPS estimates of $4.43 (down 6.3%) and revenues of $3.64 billion (down 6.5%). With a negative Earnings ESP of -0.56% and Zacks Rank #3, the stock is not considered a compelling earnings-beat candidate. In contrast, Nasdaq is expected to report earnings growth of 15.9% and has a positive Earnings ESP of +0.14%, making it more likely to beat consensus estimates.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Expected year-over-year decline in both earnings (-6.3%) and revenues (-6.5%). Negative Earnings ESP of -0.56% indicates recent analyst downgrades. Combined with Zacks Rank #3, the stock is not positioned as a compelling earnings-beat candidate. However, the company has beaten estimates in 3 of the last 4 quarters.

Expected strong year-over-year earnings growth of +15.9% and revenue growth of +11.7%. Positive Earnings ESP of +0.14% combined with Zacks Rank #3 suggests the company is likely to beat consensus EPS estimates. The company has beaten consensus estimates in all trailing four quarters.

title: Prediction: Here's What $1,000 Invested in Tesla Stock Will Be Worth in 3 Years
author: Will Ebiefung
description: Tesla's new Roadster with advanced features generates buzz but won't significantly impact revenue. While the company shows innovation, its P/E ratio of 352 is extremely expensive compared to the S&P 500's average of 24. Tesla faces margin pressures from price cuts and heavy R&D spending, with operating income down 57% in Q2. The stock is in limbo—valuation is too high for meaningful growth, but future projects like robotaxi services may sustain investor optimism for a few more years.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Tesla demonstrates strong innovation and revenue growth (+26% YoY), but faces significant headwinds: extremely high P/E ratio (352 vs S&P 500's 24), deteriorating margins, operating income down 57%, and intense competition. Future projects like robotaxi offer potential but are unproven. The article concludes a $1,000 investment is unlikely to deliver meaningful returns over 3 years unless new information emerges.
Mentioned only as a source of analyst estimates regarding Tesla's robotaxi revenue potential by 2030. No direct investment thesis or sentiment is provided.

title: Buyouts & Shareholder Yields Benefit SPGI Amid Fierce Competition
author: Na
description: S&P Global reported Q2 2026 adjusted EPS of $4.83, up 23% YoY and beating consensus by 7.6%, with pro-forma revenues rising 11% to $3.68B. The company raised its 2026 share buyback target to over $7B and achieved nearly 60% of its $100M AI-driven cost savings target. However, rising competition, AI-driven shifts in customer demand, and potential pricing pressure in credit ratings and market data could challenge future growth and margins.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong Q2 earnings beat (23% EPS growth), revenue growth of 11%, margin expansion of 200 bps, significant AI-driven cost savings, and increased capital returns through $7B+ buyback target demonstrate solid operational performance and shareholder value creation.
Q4 FY2026 earnings of $3.29 per share beat consensus by 3.1%, with 9% YoY earnings growth and 6% revenue growth, indicating strong business performance.
Q4 FY2026 adjusted earnings of $4.52 per share beat consensus by 4.6%, with 11.6% YoY earnings growth and 6.3% revenue growth, showing solid operational results.

title: CME vs. Coinbase Global: Which Financial Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
author: Erin Kennedy
description: CME Group and Coinbase Global represent two different approaches to financial infrastructure. CME operates a high-margin derivatives marketplace with a 62% net margin and strong cash generation, while Coinbase scales rapidly in crypto trading but faces regulatory uncertainty. The author recommends CME due to its superior profitability, lower valuation multiple, dividend payment, and skepticism about crypto's fundamental value.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong financial metrics with 62% net margin, low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.1, $4.2B free cash flow, dividend payment of $5.15, and lower forward P/E ratio of 23.56. Author explicitly recommends CME as the better investment choice.

While revenue growth is solid at 9.4%, the company faces high regulatory uncertainty, heavy reliance on volatile Bitcoin and Ethereum prices, lower net margin of 17.6%, and high stock-based compensation at 34.6% of operating cash flow. Author dismisses crypto as lacking intrinsic value and views it as a 'greater fool' investment.
